# Save your clean data {#sec-export}

::: {.pkgs}
Packages: `readr` `here`
:::

survey_raw has been modified in place at every step so far — this is the one point where it gets a new name. Calling it survey_clean here marks it as finished: ready for analysis, not to be edited by hand. The goal of reproducible cleaning is that you could delete survey_clean.csv entirely and regenerate it perfectly by re-running your script.

```r
library(readr)
library(here)

survey_clean <- survey_raw

write_csv(survey_clean, here("data", "clean", "survey_clean.csv"))
```

::: {.callout-tip}
Never hand-edit survey_clean.csv. If you spot an error, fix it in the cleaning script and re-run the whole thing from the raw file. Keeping raw and clean files in separate folders (data/raw/ vs data/clean/) makes it obvious at a glance which file is safe to overwrite.
:::

::: {.next-steps}
**Done.** That's the end of this path — your data should now be ready to analyse.
:::
